feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Political rivals implicated under Pakistan's anti-terror law
entry.summary: Pakistan's political showdown continues as more opposition figures are implicated under Pakistan's anti-terror law.

entry.title: Congress reacts to executive order exempting Russia from economic sanctions
entry.summary: NPR's Eric McDaniel reports on how Congress has reacted to President Trump's executive order exempting Russia from economic sanctions.

entry.title: Disgruntled farmers may help flip Senate seat in Kansas
entry.summary: President Trump heads to Kansas to campaign for Republican candidates Monday but farmers disgruntled by White House policies may help flip a U.S. Senate seat that Republicans have held for almost a century.

entry.title: What time is it on the moon?
entry.summary: James Olthoff, a delegate to the International Bureau of Weights and Measures, talks to NPR's Joel Rose about why it's important to accurately measure time on the moon.

entry.title: 'Life is absolutely brutal in Gaza,' says World Food Programme head
entry.summary: The UN's World Food Programme says 1.4 million people in Gaza are suffering acute food shortages and that funding gaps are forcing cutbacks in critical aid, despite the U.S. brokered Hamas-Israel ceasefire.

entry.title: Zoe Kazan on her adaptation of Steinbeck's East of Eden - and her grandfather's
entry.summary: Screenwriter Zoe Kazan talks about her adaptation of John Steinbeck's 1952 novel – a sprawling multigenerational epic that explores the nature of good and evil - streaming now on Netflix.

entry.title: For decades, horror films have been infused with queer themes
entry.summary: NPR's Mallory Yu, Ryan Benk and Joel Rose discuss how queer themes and characters have long found a home in horror films.

entry.title: Noah Adams, longtime host of NPR's All Things Considered, has died
entry.summary: One of NPR's most gifted storytellers, his soft voice and vivid writing helped define the network's sound for a generation of Americans.

entry.title: Oregon governor Tina Kotek reacts to Silver Rail Elementary school shooting
entry.summary: NPR's Joel Rose talks with Oregon Governor Tina Kotek about the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon.

entry.title: Student protests widen into greater social unrest in France
entry.summary: Hundreds of protests took place in cities across France. Most of them were peaceful but some turned chaotic and violent.
